A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Capacity-Aware Inference work. All 26 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, support comparison; relocated analyses and renumbered displays can be matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original language and multimodal benchmark evaluations, inference speed measurements, routing analyses and capacity-factor ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds device-level capacity experiments, long-context and generation evaluations, gating-score analysis and workload sensitivity measurements.

M1.justification: v4 Section 5.2 adds device-level capacity-aware inference alongside the retained expert-level methods. It constrains the aggregate load of local experts, allowing an individual expert to exceed its former budget when the device has spare capacity. This changes a central routing constraint; the original Token Drop and Expanded Drop procedures otherwise remain intact.

E1.justification: v4 Appendix B adds BANKING77 intent classification with long in-context demonstrations, HumanEval code generation, NQ-Open question answering and MTS-Dialog generation. These introduce distinct tasks, domains and context conditions beyond v2's retained language benchmarks and MME, MMBench and SEED-Bench evaluations.

E2.justification: The matched comparisons retain the unconstrained baseline, Order, Reverse Order, Random and Score strategies, and Expert Drop. The new benchmark evaluations reuse the baseline and proposed methods. Removing expert-pruning citations does not remove Expert Drop from Table 2; the device-level addition is a proposed-method variant.

E3.justification: v4 adds Qwen3-MoE experiments comparing expert-level gamma = 1.5 with device-level gamma = 1.0, a multiple-experts-per-GPU Mixtral configuration, and a batch-size/prompt-length sweep. Appendix B adds 100 sampled BANKING77 examples with 1–5 demonstrations per label, plus generation evaluations at gamma = 1.0 using pass@1, exact match and BERTScore. Existing language-task shot counts and metrics remain unchanged. The longest BANKING77 context is inconsistently specified as 14K in prose and 11K in Table 6.

E4.justification: v4 adds analysis of ranked gating-score distributions in Figure 8, capacity-granularity comparisons in Table 3, and workload sensitivity in Table 10 and the expanded Figure 5. These investigate routing relevance and deployment-dependent efficiency. The earlier capacity-factor, model-imbalance and maximum-selected-expert ablations are retained and consolidated in Appendix D.

E5.justification: Both Table 1 captions report averaging over multiple random seeds without specifying counts, seed values, confidence intervals or significance tests. v4 does not change this experimental uncertainty reporting. Its new gating-score mean and min–max plot describes variability across tokens, rather than uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: v4 adds results in Tables 3, 6, 7 and 10. Table 3 reports average scores of 74.8 for device-level gamma = 1.0 and 73.9 for expert-level gamma = 1.5, representing different operating points. Figure 5 adds Mixtral multi-expert speedups of 1.54× and 1.51×. Figure 4 changes DeepSeek-V2-Lite Expanded Drop at gamma = 2.0 from 1.06× to 1.09×. The retained language tables, multimodal results and full-page appendix load/drop plots remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v4 formalizes a new aggregate constraint, N1 + ... + Nnl <= nl × gamma × mean load, permitting allocations excluded by individual expert bounds. This is a limited extension of the mathematical formulation. The existing routing equations, load bounds and dropped-token expression are retained; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims about inference-time stragglers, Token Drop, Expanded Drop and efficient language/multimodal inference. The headline Mixtral claim of a 0.2% average performance improvement and 1.85× speedup is unchanged. The additional variant and experiments do not materially redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v4 adds a flat-tail gating-score explanation for why additional experts can remain relevant, identifies wasted device capacity as a limitation of individual expert caps, and interprets workload-dependent speedups through GPU utilization. Appendix B also extends applicability interpretations to long contexts and generation. Existing explanations concerning image-token redundancy and overly aggressive dropping remain.

D1.justification: v4 newly specifies the main timing workload as batch size 8K and sequence length 512; this is disclosure, not evidence of a changed earlier experiment. Appendix E replaces pseudocode with explicit PyTorch functions, including integer capacities, device placement and consistent score variables. The abstract adds a repository link and release statement, although Section 8 still describes future release plans; external availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations supporting Qwen3 and the new long-context/generation benchmarks. It removes the expert-pruning/compression references by Lu et al. and He et al. and their accompanying positioning paragraph in Section 5.2. The main related-work discussion remains substantially unchanged; citation-style conversion and the duplicated OpenBookQA reference do not represent new research coverage.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. v4 moves Section 5.4 into a consolidated ablation appendix, reorders appendix material, adds ethics and reproducibility statements, and makes localized explanatory and caption edits. This is limited restructuring rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v4 adds four result tables and a gating-score figure, expands Figure 5 with additional bars and revised legends/axis extent, and presents the algorithms as side-by-side code listings. Tables are reformatted, ablation displays move into the appendix, and the conference template changes typography and layout throughout. Most existing plotted data are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens practical validation through workload measurements and long-context/generation tests, while the device-level variant addresses wasted capacity when several experts share a GPU. Clearer implementation listings also help reproducibility. These are useful gains over v2's already substantial evaluation, but their strength is limited by unequal capacity factors in the device comparison, the 11K/14K context inconsistency, and incomplete experimental uncertainty and release documentation. The evidence supports a positive but limited overall quality improvement.
